THE RULES OF THIS BOARD — permanent, they never come off

  1. Your list goes up here first. Every item you raise becomes a card with a BEFORE picture, an AFTER picture and how I would fix it. Nothing is written into the planner before that.
  2. No code before you approve the card. You approve card by card. Only when you say “make it live” do I write anything.
  3. Approved is not live. A card you approve stays here as APPROVED until the build ships, so you can see what is queued.
  4. A card never leaves until you say remove. This board is the record of what you asked for, not a list of what I finished.
  5. Your words are kept, all of them. Your first quote stays at the top of the card forever; every later comment is added underneath it with its date, even when it repeats. I never replace what you said with my summary.
  6. The AFTER must show what it will actually look like. Never the same picture twice. If nothing is built yet, the card says so in plain words instead of pretending.
  7. Every question sits inside the problem it belongs to — never collected somewhere else. You read one card and answer it there.
  8. I raise what you have not thought of. Every card carries an I also thought of note: the thing your request does not decide — the crowded case, the phone, what happens to what you already have.
  9. I test it in Safari myself — before I call it done, and again after it goes live.
  10. Pictures, not paragraphs. Short words around the picture, never an essay above it.

How to answer: say the card number and what you want — “4 approve”, “6 I was on Week”, “14 close it”. Anything you do not mention, I leave alone. Each card has a YOUR ANSWER line at its foot showing exactly what to say.

Reminders that keep reminding until you acknowledge

NOT LIVE

2026-09-25 "let me know how you want to set that up. In the after picture, you set up the same exact picture as the before. It should be how it would look like every single time that I don't acknowledge it, and show me the process."

the cause, measured, and how I fix it

You asked how I would set it up, so here it is in full.

1. When the reminder is due it appears as it does now.
2. If you do nothing, it comes back at 5 minutes, then 15, then 30 — widening, so it nags less as time goes on rather than more.
3. Each repeat looks different from the first. It carries a count — “2nd reminder · due 25 min ago” — so you can tell at a glance this is not a fresh one.
4. It stops after one hour and leaves a quiet marker on the item, so nothing nags you forever but nothing vanishes silently either.
5. Acknowledging means pressing Got it (stops it) or Snooze (restarts the ladder). Opening the task also counts — if you acted on it, you acknowledged it.
6. Coming back after being away: ONE catch-up line, “tried 4 times”, never four stacked pop-ups.

The honest limit: this only fires while a planner tab is open. A true phone alarm that fires with the planner closed is a different mechanism and I would have to price it separately — say if you want that and I will put it up as its own card.

I also thought of — you have not decided this yet

If you are away from the planner for two hours, should you come back to one catch-up notice or to every missed repeat stacked up? I would show one, saying how many times it tried. Also worth knowing: browser notifications only fire while a tab is open — a real phone alarm would need a different mechanism entirely.

what I want to check with you

Three things to settle: (a) is the 5 / 15 / 30 ladder right, or do you want it even? (b) is stopping after an hour right? (c) is “only while a tab is open” acceptable for now?hour the right point to give up? And is it acceptable that it only works while the planner is open in a tab?
